author: Jocelyn Flores
title: FBI alerts shoppers to increased cyber threats during holidays - NewsBreak
text:
By Jocelyn Flores Andy Morgan ,
4 hours ago
EL PASO, Texas ( KTSM ) — During the holiday season, online shoppers are increasingly targeted by scammers, resulting in significant financial losses each year.
Holiday scams, including non-delivery, non-payment, auction fraud, and gift card fraud, are prevalent during the shopping season.
According to the Internet Crime Complaint Center’s (IC3) 2024 report, non-payment and non-delivery scams cost people more than $785 million that year, with credit card fraud accounting for another $199 million in losses.
Special agent Jeff Reisinger with the FBI field office in El Paso joined KTSM 9 News prime-time anchor Andy Morgan for an in-studio interview on Wednesday, Dec. 10, where he discussed the current trends when it comes to cyber investigations.
“During the holiday season, there’s going to be roughly $250 billion worth of sales. Roughly 96 percent of individuals who are going to be purchasing make at least one purchase online,” said Reisinger. “We also know that 96 percent of all frauds that take place in the United States occur due to a cyber related event.”
Scammers employ various tactics, such as non-delivery scams where buyers pay for goods or services online but never receive their items.
Non-payment scams involve sellers shipping goods or services but never receiving payment.
Auction fraud occurs when a product is misrepresented on an auction site, leading to buyer disappointment.
Gift card fraud involves sellers asking for payment via pre-paid cards, only to steal the funds without delivering the purchased item.
“We want to make sure the general public is doing everything they can to stay as safe as possible by using such things as strong pass phrases, making sure they are locking down things on their computers or the cell phones, and make sure they aren’t going to be a potential victim,” said Reisinger.
To protect against these scams, individuals should practice good cybersecurity hygiene, such as avoiding suspicious links or attachments in emails and on websites.
Verifying the legitimacy of a buyer or seller before making a purchase is crucial, as is checking website URLs for security indicators like ‘https.’
Using a credit card for online shopping and monitoring statements for suspicious transactions can help safeguard against fraud.
Tracking numbers for online purchases ensure items have been shipped and allow buyers to follow the delivery process.
By staying vigilant and practicing safe online shopping habits, consumers can reduce the risk of falling victim to holiday scams and protect their finances.
